To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the transcriptomic data of fiber flax plants were used to select genes with high potential for manipulating technical fiber quality, (ii) the selected genes were localized to specific chromosomes of the flax genome, and (iii) the selected genes could be used to develop new flax cultivars with improved fiber quality.

the gene expression in developing flax fibers is associated with technical fiber quality, and the genes that have tissue and stage-specific expression in the developing flax fibers have potential for the manipulation of technical fiber properties in the breeding process.
the expression of a set of selected genes in flax fibers can be used as a predictor of fiber quality parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a pipeline for the selection of genes for the improvement of technical fiber quality in flax.
the identification of genes suitable for the improvement of flax fiber quality and their potential use in conventional and genome editing-based breeding programs.
the identification and characterization of genes that are involved in the regulation of technical fiber quality and could be used for the improvement of fiber flax cultivars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a transcriptomic-based approach could be used to identify genes that have high impact on fiber quality parameters.
the selected genes are promising targets for the improvement of flax fiber quality.
the proposed pipeline of functional genomics is a powerful tool for the development of new varieties with improved technical fiber quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the selected genes are good candidates for the manipulation of fiber quality parameters in fiber flax.
we identified genes with tissue and developmental stage-specific pattern of gene expression in developing fibers and demonstrated their association with technical fiber quality parameters.
we have identified genes that have high predictive power for technical fiber quality.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of gene expression data in the breeding of flax for fiber yield and quality could lead to the creation of new cultivars that would be suitable for the development of a wide range of fiber products, including textile, paper, and biodegradable plastics.
the use of transcriptomic data for selection of genes with potential to improve fiber quality is feasible and effective.
the transcriptome data could be used as a starting point to identify genes with potential for the improvement of fiber quality parameters.
